title: feat(idd-review-triage): defer Low-severity findings to a follow-up issue after a round-count cutoff
body:
<!-- idd-skill-authoring-publication: target=target-76f6d887cc30cc1c; anchor=kurone-kito/idd-skill#2862; set=set-4adcd6ff338c80fe; session=claude-sonnet5-95c4e29c82659dc7; token=pub-f94924b6e3518940 -->

## Background

`idd-review-triage.instructions.md`'s E4/E5 scores each PATH A item
Low/Medium/High and, for Low, recommends Reject (fixable at the agent's
discretion); there is no ceiling on how many review-fix loop rounds
(E1-E15) a PR can go through while new Low-severity findings keep
arriving. `critiqueLoop.e10NoProgressHoldAfter` (default `3`) is a
different, narrower guard: it only fires when the **same** Accepted
finding recurs without progress across consecutive E10 passes within one
fix batch -- its own "meaningful progress" carve-out explicitly does
**not** fire when each round surfaces a genuinely new finding, since that
is convergence, not stagnation, by its own stated definition. A PR where
successive rounds each raise a different, real Low-severity finding
(e.g., one advisory bot converges, then a second advisory bot's own
first review arrives after the first bot's findings are fixed, itself
finding something new) triggers no existing guard while extending
indefinitely.

Live-observed cost evidence motivating this (from a same-day
investigation, checkable via `gh api repos/kurone-kito/idd-skill/pulls/
<n>/reviews`, `user.login == copilot-pull-request-reviewer[bot]`):
Copilot review-submission counts of 11-59 per PR across
`kurone-kito/idd-skill#2018`, `#2255`, `#2264`, `#2368`, `#2403`, `#2840`.
Each review-submission count tracks one full E1-E15 loop iteration,
since E14 requests a fresh review "after every push, regardless of
reviewer state."

**Repository-owner-confirmed scope** (hearing, 2026-09-10, before this
issue was drafted): only Low-severity PATH A items are eligible for the
new deferral disposition this issue adds -- Medium and High stay fully
blocking, unchanged, matching the existing precedent in
`critiqueLoop.e10NoProgressHoldAfter`'s own text ("Do not use this stop
condition to bypass serious issues: unresolved High/Medium findings
remain blockers until fixed or explicitly redirected by a maintainer").
Default threshold: `15` rounds -- explicitly a starting point the
repository owner expects to tune once real usage data exists, not a
final calibration; document it as such rather than as a settled number.

## Proposed change

Add a new optional policy key, `critiqueLoop.deferAfterRounds` (integer,
default `15`; absent/invalid falls back to the default, matching this
repository's existing fail-safe-on-absence convention for every other
`critiqueLoop.*` key), to `schemas/policy.schema.json` and
`docs/policy-constants.md`'s critique-loop table (a new row, alongside
the existing `C-phase low-severity loop guard` /
`E10 repeated accepted finding guard` rows).

**Round counting.** Reuse the existing `review-watermark` marker instead
of introducing new state: the round count for the current claim is the
count of trusted same-claim `<!-- review-watermark: {agent-id}
{claim-id} ... -->` comments posted so far (paginated fetch, including
comments already minimized as `OUTDATED` by the existing "Hide
superseded same-claim watermarks" step -- minimizing hides a comment
from the UI, not from the API). This round is the one about to be
processed by the current E4/E5 pass (i.e., count the watermark E1 just
posted for this pass as included).

**Trigger condition, scoped to E4/E5 only.** When the round count
reaches `critiqueLoop.deferAfterRounds`, any PATH A item this pass's E4
scores **Low** severity and E5 has not yet dispositioned (a fresh item
this round, or one carried over undispositioned from an earlier round --
never an item already `Accepted` and in the E9/E10 fix loop from a prior
round, which stays governed by `critiqueLoop.e10NoProgressHoldAfter`
unchanged, not this mechanism) is dispositioned `Reject (defer)` instead
of the normal Accept/Reject judgment E5 currently applies to Low items.
This confines the new mechanism to E4/E5's initial disposition step only
-- it must not touch or duplicate `e10NoProgressHoldAfter`'s existing
domain (an already-Accepted item stuck mid-fix).

**`Reject (defer)` disposition and reply.** Reuse the existing
`**Rejected**`-prefixed reply format (`isDispositionComment` already
parses "starts with `**Rejected**`," and F2/F3 pair dispositions to
advisory comments 1:1 by count -- introducing a new top-level disposition
category would require touching that parser and gate; reusing the
existing prefix avoids it):

```text
**Rejected** — deferred to follow-up issue #<n> (round-count cutoff
reached at round <round>/<threshold>; see the issue for full reasoning):
<short per-item reason>
```

Resolve the thread immediately after replying, per E6's existing
Rejected-item rule (unchanged).

**Follow-up issue.** Bundle every item deferred at the same cutoff event
into **one** follow-up issue (not one issue per item) -- they share the
same cause (this PR's round-count cutoff) and are naturally reviewed
together. Create it via `idd-pr-submit.instructions.md` D3's existing
follow-up-issue rule ("never call `gh issue create` ... directly; use
the `issue-authoring` skill"), with:

- A `Refs #<originating-issue>` line on its own line (never `Closes`
  and never a PR reference), per that same rule.
- One acceptance-criteria bullet per deferred item, each restating the
  original finding (actor, file/line, the finding text) so the follow-up
  is actionable without needing to re-open the original PR's review
  thread.
- The distinguishing marker
  `<!-- idd-skill-authoring-defer-source: review-fix-loop-cutoff -->` in
  the body (a plain, unparameterized marker -- this issue's own scope
  does not require it to carry the originating PR/round, since the
  `Refs` line and the acceptance-criteria bullets already carry that
  context; kept minimal so `kurone-kito/idd-skill#2864` (this roadmap's
  sibling auto-release track) has a single, simple signal to key its
  narrow auto-release exception off).

This issue's own scope ends once the follow-up issue is published under
the normal Stage 1 hold (`status:authoring` applied, as usual) -- whether
that hold is then auto-released or waits for a human is
`kurone-kito/idd-skill#2864`'s separate scope; this issue must function
correctly (leaving the follow-up held for human release) even if that
companion issue has not yet merged.

## Acceptance criteria

- `critiqueLoop.deferAfterRounds` is a documented, schema-validated,
  optional integer policy key (default `15`), fail-safe on
  absence/malformed value (falls back to the default, never blocks
  triage).
- The round count for a claim is derived from existing same-claim
  `review-watermark` comments (paginated, including minimized ones) --
  no new persisted state is introduced.
- Once the round count reaches the threshold, a still-undispositioned
  Low-severity PATH A item in the current E4/E5 pass is dispositioned
  `Reject (defer)` (the `**Rejected** —` reply format above) instead of
  the normal Accept/Reject judgment; an already-Accepted item mid-fix
  from an earlier round is unaffected by this mechanism.
- Medium- and High-severity PATH A items are never affected by this
  mechanism, at any round count.
- All items deferred at one cutoff event are bundled into a single
  follow-up issue, created via the `issue-authoring` skill (never a
  direct `gh issue create`), carrying a `Refs #<originating-issue>` line,
  one acceptance-criteria bullet per deferred item, and the
  `idd-skill-authoring-defer-source: review-fix-loop-cutoff` marker.
- `docs/policy-constants.md`'s critique-loop table documents the new key,
  explicitly noting the default is a starting point subject to
  recalibration from real usage data, not a settled value.
- `node scripts/audit-docs.mjs --check` and the repository's schema
  validation tests pass after the edit.

## Candidate files

- `idd-template/.github/instructions/idd-review-triage.instructions.md`
- `.github/instructions/idd-review-triage.instructions.md` (regenerated,
  not hand-edited directly)
- `schemas/policy.schema.json`
- `idd-template/docs/policy-constants.md`
- `docs/policy-constants.md` (regenerated, not hand-edited directly)

---

_Autopilot suitability: 4 / 5 -- higher is more autopilot-suitable;
below the configured floor is human-oriented. Direction, threshold, and
severity scope confirmed explicitly by the repository owner; remaining
judgment is limited to exact instruction-text placement._
